name: MathlibAnnex.Satellite.absoluteMaximizer_base_nearMax
title: Absolute maximization forces a near-maximal base

content.display_title: Absolute maximization forces a near-maximal base
content.one_sentence_role: A dominant determinant term prevents a large deficit in the base frame.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and use reference coordinates $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm. Let $p:V\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in V).$$
Thus $p$ is a norm. We use $p$ for the model distance and $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ for reference-coordinate estimates; the two norms are allowed to coincide. A $p$-dual contraction is a continuous real linear functional $r$ satisfying $|r(x)|\le p(x)$ for every $x$. Let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be the standard coordinate vectors. For an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals on $V$, put
$$M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))_{i,j},\quad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_Fx,\quad
\mathcal U_p=\{F:\forall i,x,\ |\ell_i(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For a real number $\eta$, define the attained maximum and near-maximal set by
$$D_p=\max_{F\in\mathcal U_p}|\det M_F|>0,\qquad
\mathcal N_{p,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U_p:D_p-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}.$$
Admissibility is measured with $p$; the matrices are written in the fixed reference coordinates.

Let $J$ be a finite index set, possibly empty; choose coefficients $c_a\in V$ for $a\in J$. A configuration is a pair $Q=(F,s)$, where $F$ is a frame and $s=(s_a)_{a\in J}$ is a family of additional continuous real linear functionals, called satellites. Write
$$\Omega_p^J=\{(F,s):F\in\mathcal U_p,\ \forall a,x,\ |s_a(x)|\le p(x)\}.$$
For any real weight $w$, let $M_F[i\leftarrow r]$ replace row $i$ by $(r(e_j))_j$ and set
$$\Phi_{w,c}(F,s)=w\det M_F+\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a].$$
An absolute maximizer means a single $Q\in\Omega_p^J$ with $|\Phi_{w,c}(Q')|\le|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|$ for every $Q'\in\Omega_p^J$. It need not maximize the signed polynomial. Set
$$S_p(c)=D_p\sum_{a\in J}\sum_{i=1}^n|(c_a)_i|.$$
Suppose $\eta\ge0$, $w>0$, $S_p(c)<w\eta$, and $Q=(F,s)$ is an admissible absolute maximizer. Then $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$.
content.assumptions: The stated positive comparison constants for $p$, finiteness of $J$, nonnegative deficit, positive weight, strict budget inequality, admissibility of $Q$ and its global absolute maximality are required. There is no $\eta<D_p$ assumption in this theorem.
content.conclusion: The base frame has $|\det M_F|\ge D_p-\eta$ while remaining $p$-dual contractive. Invertibility requires the separate additional condition $\eta<D_p$.
content.proof_summary: Bound the satellite sum and compare against an attained maximum frame with zero satellites.

proof_steps.text:
**Bound every satellite contribution.** For an admissible $Q$, replacing a row by any $s_a$ leaves a $p$-dual contraction frame. Therefore each replacement determinant has absolute value at most $D_p$. Applying [the finite satellite budget estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L441-L477) to precisely these contraction rows gives
   $$\left|\sum_{a,i}(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a]\right|
   \le D_p\sum_{a,i}|(c_a)_i|=S_p(c).$$
   Since $w\ge0$, [the absolute polynomial upper bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L480-L499) yields $|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|\le w|\det M_F|+S_p(c)$.

**Use a benchmark in the same domain.** Choose a $p$-dual frame $F_*$ attaining $D_p$, and set all its satellites to zero. This comparison configuration is admissible. Its polynomial has absolute value $wD_p$. Absolute maximality of the given $Q$ gives
   $$wD_p=|\Phi_{w,c}(F_*,0)|\le|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|.$$
   This comparison uses the same weight and coefficients, without choosing a sign for the determinant.

**Exclude a deficit larger than $\eta$.** If $|\det M_F|<D_p-\eta$, positivity of $w$ and $S_p(c)<w\eta$ imply
   $$|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|\le w|\det M_F|+S_p(c)
   <w(D_p-\eta)+w\eta=wD_p,$$
   contradicting the benchmark. Thus $D_p-\eta\le|\det M_F|$. Together with $F\in\mathcal U_p$ this is near-maximal membership, the output of [the benchmark-to-near-maximal lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L502-L522).

content.lean_realization_notes: The budget is defined by [the determinant-scaled coefficient sum](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L427-L429). For later applications with $\eta>0$, [a weight dominating that budget](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L525-L533) chooses $w=S_p(c)/\eta+1$, giving $w>0$ and $w\eta=S_p(c)+\eta>S_p(c)$. This weight choice is a contextual result with the stronger positive-deficit input, not an additional assumption on this theorem.
